header.title: FlipList
header.description: FLIP reorder and filter for lists and grids. Keep stable `key`s on each child; shuffling order translates items from their previous rect, and removing a key fades it out in place while neighbors fill the gap. Change `staggerKey` to force a full enter stagger. `maintainScroll` restores the nearest scroll parent after layout. Use block, flex, or CSS grid hosts (`div`, `ul`/`li`, cards) — not HTML `table` / `tr` (exit uses `position: absolute`).

staggerKey.title: staggerKey
staggerKey.description: Changing `staggerKey` forces every remaining item through a full enter cascade (with `staggerDelay`) instead of a FLIP reorder. Shuffle still moves with FLIP; Restagger keeps the same keys and only bumps the key.

maintainScroll.title: maintainScroll
maintainScroll.description: Scroll the box, then filter with A–L / M–Z. With `maintainScroll`, the scroll parent keeps its offset so the viewport does not jump when items leave the flow.

header.title: FlipList API
header.description: Reference for props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types for `FlipList`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for reorder, grid, staggerKey, and maintainScroll.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import from `@gem-org/gemsitions/flip-list` with its `flip-list.css`, or from the root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> and forwards them to the root div, or to the child with asChild. Each keyed child is wrapped as a FLIP item. Do not use table / tr: exit sets position: absolute.

items.keys: Every item needs a stable key. Without it FLIP cannot match identity across reorder or filter.
items.host: Use block, flex, or CSS grid hosts. Avoid table / tr: absolute exit breaks table layout.
items.filter: Filtering is the consumer’s job: FlipList only animates the children it receives. The control that filters should reflect state.
items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the order snaps to the end with no interpolation.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion keeps the animation and adds gemst-ignore-reduced-motion. Only if motion is essential.
items.asChild: With asChild, pick a semantic host (ul, ol, div): that element is the FLIP container.

items.root: Root (`div` or the child with `asChild`). `position: relative`.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Written on the host from timing and distance.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global gemsitions variables the CSS uses as defaults.

state.title: State
state.description: How the animation is turned off.

items.children: List or grid items. Stable `key`s required. Block / flex / CSS grid — not `table` / `tr`.
items.asChild: Applies classes, styles, and ref to the single child. That child is the FLIP host.
items.axis: Axes to invert. `both` (default) for grids; `y` is enough for a vertical list.
items.distance: Enter / exit Y offset in px (opacity + `translate3d`). Default `8`.
items.staggerKey: When this changes, every remaining item plays a full enter stagger (not a FLIP move).
items.maintainScroll: Restores the nearest scroll parent (or window) after layout.
items.unmountOnExit: Drops filtered items immediately (skips the exit fade).
items.duration: Duration. With `{ enter, exit }`, `enter` also drives moves; `exit` filters.
items.delay: Wait before motion. Accepts `{ enter, exit }`.
items.staggerDelay: Extra delay between entering or exiting items. Moves play together unless `staggerKey`.
items.easing: Token, timing function, or `{ enter, exit }`. Move uses enter. Default `emphasized`.
items.isDisabled: Snaps to the new order with no interpolation.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Animates even when the user prefers reduced motion. Only if essential.
items.onFlip: When a FLIP / filter cycle starts playing.
items.outFlip: When it finishes, motion is disabled, or the list unmounts.
items.style: Inline styles for the root. Combined with `--gemst-flip-*`.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `div`, or the child with `asChild`).
